title: NN-AdderNet: Nonnegative and Sparse Weight Optimization Towards Ultra-Low Bitwidth AdderNet Quantization and Compression
problem: AdderNet (using sum-of-absolute-difference instead of multiplication) is efficient, but achieving low bitwidth quantization and effective model compression remains challenging, limiting deployment to resource-constrained hardware.
motivation: AdderNet offers superior hardware efficiency over CNNs, but quantization and compression are not yet optimized for the unique SAD kernel structure, limiting bitwidth reduction.
method: NN-AdderNet transforms the sum-of-absolute-difference (SAD) kernel to enable nonnegative weights, eliminating the need for sign bits (saving 1 bit per weight). It exploits dual-sparsity patterns in the quantized model weights for enhanced lossless compression. The method combines quantization-friendly weight transformation with sparse encoding.
key_novelty: Equivalent SAD transformation enabling nonnegative weights to eliminate sign bit overhead, combined with dual-sparsity exploitation for aggressive bitwidth reduction.
contributions: Equivalent SAD transformation converting signed to nonnegative weights, eliminating sign bit requirement
Dual-sparsity pattern exploitation in NN-AdderNet quantized models for enhanced compression
Compressed weight bitwidth down to 4 bits or lower while maintaining negligible accuracy loss
Both algorithmic and hardware-level efficiency improvements demonstrated with energy and latency gains in inference accelerators

metrics.other: Compressed weight bitwidth down to 4-bits or lower; negligible accuracy loss vs full-precision AdderNet

limitations: Abstract does not discuss inference latency improvement on actual hardware, comparison with other ultra-low-bitwidth quantization methods, or scalability to larger models.
primary_theme: Nonnegative weight transformation for ultra-low-bitwidth AdderNet
